definition: The logical and stylistic consistency of a generated text, measuring whether ideas flow sensibly and the output reads as a unified whole.
details: Coherence is one of several qualitative dimensions (alongside fluency, relevance, and faithfulness) commonly assessed in both human and automated evaluation of generated text.

explainer.lead: Coherence is what makes a generated text hold together rather than read like a pile of disconnected sentences. It matters because writing can be grammatically flawless and still fail to make sense as a whole.

tiers.eli5: Coherence is like a row of dominoes: each sentence should connect to the one before it and help the whole piece make sense. A story about a rainy day should not suddenly jump to dinosaurs unless there is a reason. Even perfectly written sentences can feel confusing when they do not belong together.
tiers.practitioner: Coherence is assessed during human or automated evaluation of generated text, often alongside fluency, relevance, and faithfulness. A practical check is to follow the text’s ideas and transitions, looking for abrupt topic shifts, contradictory statements, or sentences that do not support the overall point. A common pitfall is treating grammatical correctness or factual relevance as proof that the full output is coherent.
tiers.paperLevel: Coherence C(t) denotes the degree to which a generated text t exhibits logical and stylistic consistency, sensible idea flow, and unity. It is a qualitative evaluation dimension rather than a single specified formula, and can be assessed by humans or automated methods. It remains distinct from fluency, relevance, and faithfulness, so strength on one dimension does not establish strength on another.

explainer.example: “Maya planned to cycle to school. When heavy rain began, she took the bus instead” is coherent because the second sentence gives a reason for the change of plan. “Maya planned to cycle to school. Bananas are yellow. She took the bus” uses grammatical sentences, but the middle sentence breaks the logical flow.

usedIn.name: Text summarization
usedIn.detail: Checks whether a generated summary develops its ideas sensibly and reads as a unified whole.

usedIn.name: Dialogue generation
usedIn.detail: Checks whether a generated reply holds together logically instead of jumping between unrelated ideas.

usedIn.name: Natural language generation evaluation
usedIn.detail: Serves as one qualitative dimension in both human judgments and automated assessments.

explainer.intuition: Good coherence means the reader can follow how each sentence connects to the next and to the text’s overall point. It concerns both the logic of the ideas and the consistency of the writing style.
howItWorks: Read the generated text as a whole, not just sentence by sentence.
Trace whether each idea follows sensibly from earlier ideas.
Check for unexplained jumps, contradictions, or abrupt changes in style.
Judge coherence separately from fluency, relevance, and faithfulness.
explainer.whyItMatters: Coherence helps reveal generation failures that sentence-level checks can miss. Without it, an evaluation may reward text that sounds polished but is confusing or disconnected when read as a whole.
misconceptions: Coherence is not the same as fluency: grammatical sentences can still form a disjointed text.
Coherence is not the same as relevance: sentences can concern the right topic without connecting sensibly.
Coherence is not the same as faithfulness: a unified, logical text can still fail to stay faithful to its source.
